title: Cabin Pressure Outflow Valve Actuator — Removal
abstract: Removal of the outflow valve actuator, covering the single-motor and duplex installations and the second essential bus feed that must be isolated separately on the duplex standard.

sections.purpose: This task removes the outflow valve actuator so that it can be replaced, or so that the valve mechanism behind it can be examined.
sections.job_setup_note: On the duplex standard the actuator is fed from two essential buses and isolating one does not make the actuator safe. Both must be isolated and confirmed at zero before the connector is broken. Confirm the standard from the aircraft record; the two installations look similar from the front and differ only in the connector contact count.
sections.procedure: 1. Confirm that the aircraft is depressurised and that the cabin pressure system is not in test. 2. Confirm from the aircraft record whether the single-motor or the duplex actuator is fitted. 3. Isolate the actuator supply. On the duplex standard, isolate both essential bus feeds and tag both. WARNING: ON THE DUPLEX INSTALLATION, ISOLATING ONE BUS DOES NOT MAKE THE ACTUATOR SAFE. ISOLATE BOTH AND CONFIRM ZERO VOLTS AT THE CONNECTOR. 4. Lift the floor panel in zone 165 and gain access to the actuator. 5. Confirm zero volts at every connector contact and record the reading. 6. Disconnect the actuator connector and cap it. On the duplex standard, disconnect both motor harnesses. 7. Release the cushioned loop clamps AGS958367K4 holding the second motor cable along the forward duct D2130115062812, where fitted. 8. Mark the valve position and the actuator output arm before anything is released. CAUTION: MARK THE OUTPUT ARM POSITION. THE ACTUATOR CAN BE REFITTED ONE SPLINE OUT AND THE VALVE WILL THEN NEVER REACH FULLY CLOSED. 9. Release the coupling at the valve shaft. 10. Release the four actuator mounting fasteners and support the actuator. 11. Withdraw the actuator clear and put it on a clean surface. 12. Where the accumulator D2130117925957 must be disturbed for access, record its charge pressure before it is depressurised. 13. Check the filter 141HM and the manifold 6820HQ in the lower position while access is available.
sections.close_out: Cap the connector or connectors and cover the valve shaft. Record the marked output arm position, the accumulator charge pressure where it was disturbed, and the isolation tags fitted. Do not leave the floor panel out overnight without a barrier.

type_data.effectivity_note: All aircraft; steps 3, 6 and 7 differ between the single-motor and the duplex installation

safety_precautions: Isolate both essential bus feeds on the duplex installation.
Mark the output arm before releasing the coupling.

title: Cabin Pressure Outflow Valve Actuator — Removal

issue.reason: The access panel list is split by aircraft: the four-engine floor arrangement reaches the actuator from the inboard avionics bay and the lower cabin, not from the panels used on the twin-engine aircraft.

abstract: Removal of the outflow valve actuator, covering the single-motor and duplex installations, the second essential bus feed that must be isolated separately, and the two access routes the twin-engine and four-engine floors need.

sections.purpose: This task removes the outflow valve actuator so that it can be replaced, or so that the valve mechanism behind it can be examined.
sections.job_setup_note: On the duplex standard the actuator is fed from two essential buses and isolating one does not make the actuator safe. Both must be isolated and confirmed at zero before the connector is broken. Confirm the standard from the aircraft record; the two installations look similar from the front and differ only in the connector contact count. Confirm the access route as well. The four-engine aircraft carries the avionics bay divider one frame further aft, so the outboard panels used on the twin-engine aircraft do not reach the actuator and the route is through the inboard bay and the lower cabin instead.
sections.procedure: 1. Confirm that the aircraft is depressurised and that the cabin pressure system is not in test. 2. Confirm from the aircraft record whether the single-motor or the duplex actuator is fitted, and whether the aircraft is twin-engine or four-engine. 3. Isolate the actuator supply. On the duplex standard, isolate both essential bus feeds and tag both. WARNING: ON THE DUPLEX INSTALLATION, ISOLATING ONE BUS DOES NOT MAKE THE ACTUATOR SAFE. ISOLATE BOTH AND CONFIRM ZERO VOLTS AT THE CONNECTOR. 4. On the twin-engine aircraft, lift the floor panel in zone 165 through panels 165CL and 242AR and gain access to the actuator. On the four-engine aircraft, open panels 166BL and 166BR in the inboard avionics bay and drop the lower cabin panel 243BR; the actuator is then reached from below and the floor panel in zone 165 is not lifted. 5. Confirm zero volts at every connector contact and record the reading. 6. Disconnect the actuator connector and cap it. On the duplex standard, disconnect both motor harnesses. 7. Release the cushioned loop clamps AGS958367K4 holding the second motor cable along the forward duct D2130115062812, where fitted. On the four-engine aircraft there are two further clamp positions aft of the bulkhead. 8. Mark the valve position and the actuator output arm before anything is released. CAUTION: MARK THE OUTPUT ARM POSITION. THE ACTUATOR CAN BE REFITTED ONE SPLINE OUT AND THE VALVE WILL THEN NEVER REACH FULLY CLOSED. 9. Release the coupling at the valve shaft. 10. Release the four actuator mounting fasteners and support the actuator. 11. Withdraw the actuator clear and put it on a clean surface. On the four-engine access route the actuator is withdrawn downwards and the cradle is fitted before the last fastener comes out. 12. Where the accumulator D2130117925957 must be disturbed for access, record its charge pressure before it is depressurised. 13. Check the filter 141HM and the manifold 6820HQ in the lower position while access is available.
sections.close_out: Cap the connector or connectors and cover the valve shaft. Record the marked output arm position, the accumulator charge pressure where it was disturbed, and the isolation tags fitted. Do not leave the floor panel out overnight without a barrier. On the four-engine aircraft, refit the lower cabin panel before the bay is left, because the open aperture is at head height in the aisle.

type_data.effectivity_note: All aircraft. Steps 3, 6 and 7 differ between the single-motor and the duplex installation; steps 4 and 11 differ between the twin-engine and the four-engine floor arrangement

safety_precautions: Isolate both essential bus feeds on the duplex installation.
Mark the output arm before releasing the coupling.
